name: Random Equivalence Queries Complexity
definition: For a fixed known probability distribution $\mu$ on the domain, assumed to give positive mass to every relevant disagreement set, the **Random Equivalence Queries Complexity** is the least worst-case expected number of arbitrary equivalence queries needed to identify a target in $\mathcal H$, when a failed hypothesis receives a counterexample sampled from $\mu$ conditioned on its disagreement set with the target. Thus the quantity is properly written $\mathrm Q_{\mathrm{req}}(\mathcal H;\mu)$.
graph_summary: Expected arbitrary-equivalence-query complexity under a fixed known counterexample distribution $\mu$.
comments: This is distribution-dependent rather than a pure invariant of $\mathcal H$.  No projection or conditioning comparison is asserted until a convention for transporting $\mu$ is fixed.
origin_references: Introduced by Angluin and Dohrn in \cite{angluin2017random}.

monotonic.proof: Fix $\mu$.  An arbitrary-equivalence strategy for $\mathcal H$ can be used unchanged when the target is restricted to $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal H$: for each proposed hypothesis and target, the random counterexample law depends only on their disagreement set and $\mu$, not on the ambient class.
